source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 23 (PDF 101-117, printed 98-114); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 23 (Carbonyl Compounds and Carboxylic Acids), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 The structural unit >C=O in organic chemistry is known as the:
blocks.explanation: The >C=O unit is the carbonyl group; aldehydes and ketones contain it (23.1).

book_ref.quote: the structural unit >C=O is known as carbonyl group

blocks.prompt: 2 Which two classes of compounds are called carbonyl compounds in this chapter?
blocks.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones are the classes of compounds that contain a carbonyl group (23.1).

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes and ketones are the classes of compounds that contain a carbonyl group

blocks.prompt: 3 The most common ketone, found in nail polish removers, is:
blocks.explanation: The most common ketone is acetone (propanone), found in nail polish removers (23.1).

book_ref.quote: The most common ketone is acetone, which is found in nail polish removers

blocks.prompt: 4 The smell and taste of bitter almond is due to:
blocks.explanation: The smell and taste of bitter almond is due to benzaldehyde, C₆H₅CHO (23.1, Interesting Information).

book_ref.quote: The smell and taste of bitter almond is due to benzaldehyde

blocks.prompt: 5 According to the chapter, aldehydes are present in:

options.text: many spices, fruits and natural fragrances

blocks.explanation: Aldehydes are present in many spices, fruits and natural fragrances; ketones are used in pharmaceuticals, chemicals and paint industries (23.1).

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes are present in many spices, fruits, and natural fragrances

blocks.prompt: 6 Propan-1-ol is warmed with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ and the product is distilled off as it forms. The product is:
blocks.explanation: Aldehydes are prepared by oxidising primary alcohols with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or acidified KMnO₄ (23.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes are prepared by the oxidation of primary alcohols with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or acidified KMnO₄.

blocks.prompt: 7 In the preparation of ethanal from ethanol, the ethanal is distilled off as soon as it is formed in order to:

options.text: increase the rate of oxidation of ethanol
prevent its further oxidation to ethanoic acid

blocks.explanation: Distilling off the aldehyde as soon as it forms prevents the further oxidation of ethanal to ethanoic acid (23.1.1).

book_ref.quote: The aldehyde produced is distilled off as soon as it is formed.

blocks.prompt: 8 During the preparation of ethanal, the temperature of the reaction mixture is kept:

options.text: below the boiling points of both ethanal and ethanol
above the boiling points of both
above the boiling point of ethanal but below that of ethanol

blocks.explanation: The temperature is kept above the b.p. of acetaldehyde (ethanal) but below that of ethanol, so only ethanal distils off (23.1.1).

book_ref.quote: The temperature is kept above the boiling point of acetaldehyde but below to that of ethanol

blocks.prompt: 9 In the preparation of a ketone from a secondary alcohol, the ketone is not distilled off immediately because:

options.text: ketones are gases at room temperature
ketones are not converted into carboxylic acids under these conditions
ketones react with K₂Cr₂O₇ to give alcohols

blocks.explanation: Ketones are not converted into carboxylic acids under these conditions, so there is no need to remove them at once (23.1.1).

book_ref.quote: since ketones are not converted into carboxylic acids under these conditions

blocks.prompt: 10 Formalin, used for preserving biological specimens, is about a 40 % aqueous solution of:
blocks.explanation: HCHO is methanal (formaldehyde), a gas at room temperature, met as 40 % formalin (23.1.1, with the book correction: not methanol).

book_ref.quote: It is often encountered as a 40 % aqueous solution called 'formalin'

blocks.prompt: 11 At room temperature, methanal is a gas while other short-chain aldehydes and ketones are:
blocks.explanation: Methanal is a gas; other short-chain aldehydes and ketones are liquids (23.1.1).

book_ref.quote: Other short-chain aldehydes and ketones are liquids.

blocks.prompt: 12 Oxidation of propan-2-ol with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ gives:
blocks.explanation: Ketones are prepared by the oxidation of secondary alcohols: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ + [O] → CH₃COCH₃ + H₂O (23.1.2).

book_ref.quote: Ketones are prepared by the oxidation of secondary alcohols.

blocks.prompt: 13 The two basic types of reactions of carbonyl compounds named in the chapter are:

options.text: nucleophilic addition reactions and alpha (α) carbon specific reactions

blocks.explanation: The >C=O group governs their chemistry; the two basic reactions are nucleophilic addition and α-carbon specific reactions (23.2).

book_ref.quote: governs the chemistry of aldehydes and ketones

blocks.prompt: 14 In the carbonyl group, the sp² hybridized carbon is bonded to:

options.text: oxygen by a double bond and two other groups by single bonds
oxygen by a single bond and three groups by single bonds
oxygen by a triple bond and one other group
two oxygen atoms by double bonds

blocks.explanation: Both C and O are sp²; carbon is bonded to oxygen through a double bond and to two other groups through single bonds (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: both carbon and oxygen are sp² hybridized

blocks.prompt: 15 The carbonyl group is polar because:

options.text: carbon is more electronegative than oxygen
it has a lone pair on carbon
oxygen is more electronegative and gets δ⁻ while carbon gets δ⁺

blocks.explanation: Oxygen, being more electronegative, gets a partial negative charge and carbon a partial positive charge (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: Carbonyl group is polar in nature because oxygen, being more electronegative

blocks.prompt: 16 The carbonyl carbon is attacked by:
blocks.explanation: Due to its δ⁺ charge the carbonyl carbon is electrophilic and is attacked by nucleophiles (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: The carbonyl carbon is electrophilic in nature due to its δ⁺ charge

blocks.prompt: 17 Which feature makes the carbonyl carbon uncrowded and supports addition reactions?

options.text: the planar shape of the group
the tetrahedral shape of the group
the presence of a triple bond

blocks.explanation: The π bond is easily broken, and the planar shape makes the carbonyl carbon uncrowded, supporting addition (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: planar shape of the group makes the carbonyl carbon uncrowded

blocks.prompt: 18 The C=O double bond undergoes addition reactions mainly because:

options.text: its σ bond is very weak
its π bond is easily broken

blocks.explanation: The double bond can undergo addition because the π bond is easily broken (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: The double bond can undergo addition reactions because π bond is easily broken down.

blocks.prompt: 19 Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones towards nucleophiles because in ketones:

options.text: the carbonyl carbon carries more positive charge
the oxygen atom is sp³ hybridized
two alkyl groups reduce the δ⁺ on carbon and cause steric hindrance

blocks.explanation: In a ketone the +I effect of two alkyl groups reduces the positive charge on carbon, and the two groups get in the way of the nucleophile (steric hindrance) (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones for two reasons.

blocks.prompt: 20 The blocking of an attacking nucleophile by the two alkyl groups of a ketone is called:
blocks.explanation: The two alkyl groups of a ketone tend to get in the way of attacking nucleophiles; this is steric hindrance (23.2.1).

book_ref.quote: This is also called steric hindrance.

blocks.prompt: 21 The correct IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CHCOCH₂CH₃ is:
blocks.explanation: Numbering from the end nearer the C=O and the branch gives 2-methylpentan-3-one (23.2.1, book correction: not 4-methylpentan-3-one).

book_ref.quote: so the compound (CH₃)₂CHCOCH₂CH₃ is 2-methylpentan-3-one

blocks.prompt: 22 Aldehydes and ketones react with hydrogen cyanide to form:
blocks.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones add HCN to form cyanohydrins (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes and ketones react with hydrogen cyanide to form cyanohydrins.

blocks.prompt: 23 HCN is not used directly in the addition reaction because:

options.text: it does not react with aldehydes
it is an extremely poisonous gas

blocks.explanation: HCN is an extremely poisonous gas, so it is produced in the mixture by slowly adding HCl to NaCN or KCN with the carbonyl compound (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: HCN itself is not used directly as it is an extremely poisonous gas.

blocks.prompt: 24 A slight excess of KCN is added in the HCN addition so that:

options.text: free CN⁻ ions are present to start and catalyse the reaction

blocks.explanation: HCN is neither a nucleophile nor a strong acid, so a slight excess of KCN gives free CN⁻ ions that start and catalyse the reaction (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: This is done by adding a slight excess of KCN

blocks.prompt: 25 HCN itself does not act as a nucleophile because:

options.text: its carbon atom has no lone pair

blocks.explanation: HCN is not a nucleophile (no lone pair on its carbon) and is not a strong acid, so it gives too little CN⁻ (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: HCN is neither a nucleophile (absence of a lone pair on the carbon atom)

blocks.prompt: 26 About cyanohydrin formation, which statement is correct?

options.text: the equilibria lie far to the left
the yield of cyanohydrin is always very low
both steps are reversible but the equilibria lie far to the right

blocks.explanation: Both steps are reversible, but the equilibria lie far to the right, giving high yields (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Although both the steps involved in cyanohydrin formation are reversible

blocks.prompt: 27 The cyanohydrin used as an intermediate in the manufacture of Perspex is formed from HCN and:
blocks.explanation: Propanone + HCN gives (CH₃)₂C(OH)CN, 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile, the Perspex intermediate (23.3.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: The Perspex intermediate is the product of propanone and HCN drawn below

blocks.prompt: 28 The product of ethanal with HCN is:
blocks.explanation: CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN, 2-hydroxypropanenitrile (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Ethanal and HCN give 2-hydroxypropanenitrile

blocks.prompt: 29 Nitriles (such as cyanohydrins) on hydrolysis with dilute acid give:
blocks.explanation: Nitriles are hydrolysed by dilute acid or aqueous alkali to carboxylic acids or carboxylate ions (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Nitriles are hydrolysed by dilute acid or aqueous alkali

blocks.prompt: 30 Reduction of propanal with NaBH₄ gives:
blocks.explanation: With NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄, aldehydes give primary alcohols, so propanal gives propan-1-ol (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: aldehydes give primary alcohols and ketones gives secondary alcohols

blocks.prompt: 31 Reduction of butanone (CH₃COCH₂CH₃) with LiAlH₄ gives:
blocks.explanation: Ketones are reduced by NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄ to secondary alcohols (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: With a reducing agent such as NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄

blocks.prompt: 32 In the reduction equations, the symbol [H] represents:

options.text: reducing H coming from NaBH₄, not atomic hydrogen

blocks.explanation: [H] is the reducing H from NaBH₄ written to balance the equation; it does not represent atomic hydrogen (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Notice that reducing H in brackets [ ] comes from NaBH₄ to balance the equation.

blocks.prompt: 33 The nucleophile that attacks the carbonyl carbon in the reduction by NaBH₄ is the:
blocks.explanation: The reduction is the addition of the hydride ion (H⁻) to the carbonyl carbon (23.3.1, heading 2).

book_ref.quote: Since aldehydes and ketones are synthesised by oxidation of alcohols

blocks.prompt: 34 Aldehydes and ketones react with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine to give:

options.text: orange crystalline solids with well-defined melting points

blocks.explanation: The condensation with 2,4-DNPH gives orange crystalline solids with well-defined melting points (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: to give an orange crystalline solids with well-defined melting points

blocks.prompt: 35 The reaction of a carbonyl compound with 2,4-DNPH is of the type:
blocks.explanation: It is an addition-elimination (condensation) reaction; water is eliminated (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Addition of 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (Addition – elimination / Condensation Reaction)

blocks.prompt: 36 Which of the following, although it contains the >C=O group, does NOT give the 2,4-DNPH test?
blocks.explanation: Carboxylic acids, esters, acyl halides and amides contain >C=O but do not give this test (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: which also contain the carbonyl group >C=O do not give this test

blocks.prompt: 37 The orange crystals obtained from ethanal and 2,4-DNPH are:
blocks.explanation: 2,4-DNPH is the reagent; the orange crystals are ethanal 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone (23.3.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: the orange crystals are the product, ethanal 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone

blocks.prompt: 38 Besides water, the other product of ethanal with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine is a:
blocks.explanation: Ethanal + 2,4-DNPH → ethanal 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone + H₂O; the reagent identifies carbonyl compounds (23.3.1).

book_ref.quote: This reagent is used to identify carbonyl compounds.

blocks.prompt: 39 Ketones are reluctant towards oxidation because:

options.text: a C-C bond has to be broken during their oxidation
their carbonyl carbon has a hydrogen atom

blocks.explanation: A C-C bond has to be broken to oxidise a ketone, so only strong oxidising agents oxidise ketones (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: because C-C bond has to be broken down during oxidation

blocks.prompt: 40 Which statement about oxidation of carbonyl compounds is correct?

options.text: ketones are oxidised by weak oxidising agents
aldehydes are oxidised only by strong oxidising agents
neither is oxidised to an acid
aldehydes are oxidised by both weak and strong oxidising agents

blocks.explanation: Aldehydes are oxidised by both weak and strong oxidising agents; ketones only by strong ones (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: whereas aldehydes are oxidized by both weak and strong oxidizing agents

blocks.prompt: 41 Tollens' reagent is:
blocks.explanation: Tollens' reagent, ammoniacal silver nitrate, contains silver ions in aqueous alkaline solution (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Tollen's reagent also called ammonical silver nitrate solution

blocks.prompt: 42 On gentle warming with an aldehyde, Tollens' reagent gives:

options.text: a silver mirror on the wall of the test tube

blocks.explanation: The Ag⁺ ions are reduced to silver metal, forming a silver mirror along the wall of the tube (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: A silver mirror is formed along the wall of the test tube.

blocks.prompt: 43 Which substance was used with Tollens' reagent to make mirrors for domestic use?
blocks.explanation: A dilute solution of glucose (an aldehydic sugar) was used to make mirrors by the silver mirror reaction (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: A dilute solution of the glucose (aldehydic sugar) was used to make mirrors

blocks.prompt: 44 In Fehling's test, the brick-red precipitate formed with an aldehyde is:
blocks.explanation: Cu²⁺ ions are reduced to Cu⁺, which in alkaline solution form a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: the Cu²⁺ ions are reduced to Cu¹⁺ ions

blocks.prompt: 45 In Fehling's solution, the Cu²⁺ ions in aqueous alkaline medium are complexed with:
blocks.explanation: Fehling's solution is bright blue Cu²⁺ in alkaline medium complexed with a salt of tartaric acid (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: complexed with salt of tartaric acid

blocks.prompt: 46 Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test?
blocks.explanation: Only aldehydes reduce Tollens' reagent; ketones do not give this test (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Ketones do not give this test.

blocks.prompt: 47 Among aldehydes, the only one that gives the iodoform test is:
blocks.explanation: Among aldehydes only ethanal, and among ketones only methyl ketones, possess the CH₃CO- (acetyl) group (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Among aldehydes, only ethanal and among ketones, only methyl ketones possess the group CH₃CO-

blocks.prompt: 48 Iodoform, formed in the iodoform test, is:
blocks.explanation: CH₃CO- compounds with I₂ and NaOH give triiodomethane (CHI₃), a yellow crystalline solid called iodoform (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: a yellow crystalline solid called iodoform

blocks.prompt: 49 Which of the following ketones gives the iodoform test?
blocks.explanation: Only methyl ketones (CH₃CO- group) give yellow iodoform; butanone is a methyl ketone (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Hence, the appearance of yellow precipitates will identify the presence of CH₃CO- group

blocks.prompt: 50 In the iodoform reaction of propanone with I₂ and NaOH, the salt formed along with CHI₃ and NaI is:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COCH₃ + 3I₂ + 4NaOH → CHI₃ + CH₃COO⁻Na⁺ + 3NaI + 3H₂O (23.3.2, book correction).

book_ref.quote: For acetone (propanone) the salt formed is sodium ethanoate, not sodium methanoate

blocks.prompt: 51 Ethanol gives the iodoform test because:

options.text: it contains a CH₃-CH₂-O group that acts like a ketone
iodine in alkali first oxidises it to ethanal, which has the CH₃-C=O group

blocks.explanation: Ethanol has the CH₃-CH(OH)- group; I₂/NaOH first oxidises it to ethanal, which then gives iodoform (23.3.2, book correction).

book_ref.quote: Ethanol also gives this test, while methanol does not.

blocks.prompt: 52 Which of the following alcohols gives the iodoform test?
blocks.explanation: Alcohols with the CH₃-CH(OH)- group give the test; methanol cannot give a CH₃-C=O compound (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: alcohols having CH3-CH(OH) group give iodoform test

blocks.prompt: 53 Halogens readily substitute hydrogen in aldehydes and ketones at the:
blocks.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones undergo substitution by halogens readily at the alpha position, which is the basis of the iodoform test (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes and ketones undergo substitution reactions by halogens readily at alpha position.

blocks.prompt: 54 In the Tollens' test, the aldehyde acts as:
blocks.explanation: The aldehyde reduces Ag⁺ to silver metal and is itself oxidised, so it is the reducing agent (23.3.2).

book_ref.quote: These silver ions are readily reduced to silver metal on gentle warming with an aldehyde.

blocks.prompt: 55 In CH₃CHO + 3I₂ + 4NaOH → CHI₃ + HCOONa + 3NaI + 3H₂O, the number of moles of NaOH needed for 0.5 mol of ethanal is:
blocks.explanation: Mole ratio CH₃CHO : NaOH = 1 : 4, so 0.5 × 4 = 2.0 mol NaOH (23.3.2 equation).

book_ref.quote: These compounds react with iodine in the presence of sodium hydroxide

blocks.prompt: 56 The functional group of carboxylic acids is:
blocks.explanation: Carboxylic acids have the carboxyl functional group -COOH (23.4).

book_ref.quote: Carboxylic acids are the organic compounds having the carboxyl functional group (-COOH)

blocks.prompt: 57 The carboxylic acid found in ants is:
blocks.explanation: Methanoic acid (formic acid) is found in ants (23.4).

book_ref.quote: methanoic acid (formic acid, found in ants)

blocks.prompt: 58 The acid present in rancid butter is:
blocks.explanation: Butanoic acid (butyric acid) is in rancid butter; ethanoic acid is in vinegar (23.4).

book_ref.quote: butanoic acid (butyric acid, in the rancid butter)

blocks.prompt: 59 Lower carboxylic acids have high boiling points because of:
blocks.explanation: Lower carboxylic acids are liquids with high boiling points due to their ability to form hydrogen bonds (23.4).

book_ref.quote: This is due to their ability to make the hydrogen bond.

blocks.prompt: 60 The melting point and boiling point of ethanoic acid given in the chapter are:
blocks.explanation: Ethanoic acid melts at 17 °C and boils at 118 °C (23.4).

book_ref.quote: The melting point of ethanoic acid is 17 °C, and its boiling point is 118 °C.

blocks.prompt: 61 Pure solid ethanoic acid is called glacial acetic acid because:
blocks.explanation: Its m.p. (17 °C) is close to room temperature, so it solidifies in winter; the solid resembles glaciers (23.4).

book_ref.quote: The solid form of pure ethanoic acid is called glacial acetic acid

blocks.prompt: 62 Two molecules of acetic acid join to form a dimer through:
blocks.explanation: Acetic acid forms a dimeric form due to hydrogen bonding (23.4).

book_ref.quote: Dimeric form of acetic acid formed due to the hydrogen bonding

blocks.prompt: 63 Long chain aliphatic monocarboxylic acids are called:
blocks.explanation: Long chain aliphatic monocarboxylic acids are fatty acids, e.g. stearic, palmitic and oleic acids (23.4).

book_ref.quote: Long chain aliphatic monocarboxylic acids are called fatty acids.

blocks.prompt: 64 Fatty acids are insoluble in water because of their:
blocks.explanation: Fatty acids are insoluble in water due to their long hydrophobic alkyl chains (23.4).

book_ref.quote: They are insoluble in water due to their long hydrophobic alkyl chains.

blocks.prompt: 65 Palmitic acid has the formula C₁₆H₃₂O₂. Using C = 12, H = 1 and O = 16, its molar mass is:

book_ref.quote: Palmitic acid (C₁₆H₃₂O₂) is a long chain carboxylic acid

blocks.prompt: 66 Methanoic acid and ethanoic acid are soluble in water because they:
blocks.explanation: Due to their ability to form hydrogen bonds, the lower acids are soluble in water (23.4).

book_ref.quote: lower acids, i.e. methanoic acid and ethanoic acid are soluble in water

blocks.prompt: 67 To prepare a carboxylic acid from a primary alcohol, the alcohol is:

options.text: distilled off with a little K₂Cr₂O₇
refluxed with excess acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇

blocks.explanation: For the acid, the starting material is refluxed with excess acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇, so oxidation is complete (23.4.1).

book_ref.quote: The starting material is refluxed with excess of either acidified KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇.

blocks.prompt: 68 Hydrolysis of ethanenitrile, CH₃CN, in acidic medium gives:
blocks.explanation: Alkane nitriles are directly hydrolysed to carboxylic acids in acidic medium: CH₃CN → CH₃COOH (23.4.1).

book_ref.quote: Alkane nitriles can be directly hydrolysed to carboxylic acids in acidic medium.

blocks.prompt: 69 In alkaline hydrolysis, a nitrile first gives:

options.text: the salt of the carboxylic acid, which gives the acid on acidification

blocks.explanation: In alkaline hydrolysis nitriles first give carboxylate salts, which yield carboxylic acids on acidification (23.4.1).

book_ref.quote: In alkaline hydrolyses, they first produce salts of carboxylic acids

blocks.prompt: 70 Refluxing ethyl ethanoate with dilute acid gives:
blocks.explanation: An ester refluxed with dilute acid is hydrolysed to the carboxylic acid (and alcohol) (23.4.1).

book_ref.quote: When an ester is refluxed with either dilute acid or dilute alkali

blocks.prompt: 71 Alkaline hydrolysis of an ester with NaOH goes to completion because:

options.text: the acid formed becomes its salt

blocks.explanation: With NaOH the acid formed becomes its salt, so the reaction goes to completion (one-way arrow) (23.4.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: with NaOH the acid formed becomes its salt and the reaction goes to completion

blocks.prompt: 72 Methylbenzene is oxidised by acidified KMnO₄ to:
blocks.explanation: Methylbenzene is readily oxidised by acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇ to benzoic acid (23.4.1).

book_ref.quote: Methyl benzene is readily oxidized by acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇ to benzoic acid.

blocks.prompt: 73 The balanced equation for the oxidation of ethanal to ethanoic acid is:
blocks.explanation: CH₃CHO + [O] → CH₃COOH is balanced; the printed '+ H₂O' is a book error (23.4.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: it is CH₃CHO + [O] → CH₃COOH, as drawn above

blocks.prompt: 74 Which is NOT one of the three types of reactions of carboxylic acids listed in the chapter?

options.text: reactions involving the acidic hydrogen only
reactions involving electrophilic attack on the alkyl chain only
reactions involving replacement of the -OH group
reactions involving the carboxyl group as a whole

blocks.explanation: The three types: acidic hydrogen only, replacement of -OH, and the carboxyl group as a whole (23.5).

book_ref.quote: Those involving the carboxyl group as a whole.

blocks.prompt: 75 Carboxylic acids react with active metals and bases because they:
blocks.explanation: Carboxylic acids show considerable acidic character because they give H⁺ ions in water (23.5 A).

book_ref.quote: Carboxylic acids show considerable acidic character because they give H⁺ ions in water.

blocks.prompt: 76 The gas evolved when sodium reacts with ethanoic acid is:
blocks.explanation: 2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COO⁻Na⁺ + H₂ (23.5 A).

book_ref.quote: This why they can react with the basic species and active metals.

blocks.prompt: 77 Besides sodium ethanoate, the products of ethanoic acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate are:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COO⁻Na⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O (23.5 A, with the corrected CH₃).

book_ref.quote: With metal carbonates and bicarbonates

blocks.prompt: 78 Using 2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COO⁻Na⁺ + H₂, the moles of H₂ given by 0.40 mol of ethanoic acid with excess sodium are:
blocks.explanation: 2 mol acid give 1 mol H₂, so 0.40 / 2 = 0.20 mol H₂ (23.5 A).

book_ref.quote: The balanced equation is CH₃–COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃–COO⁻Na⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O.

blocks.prompt: 79 Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate in the ratio CH₃COOH : Na₂CO₃ =
blocks.explanation: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COO⁻Na⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O (23.5 A).

book_ref.quote: This why they can react with the basic species and active metals.

blocks.prompt: 80 Ethanoic acid reacts with SOCl₂ to give:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COOH + SOCl₂ → CH₃COCl + HCl + SO₂; the -OH group is replaced by Cl (23.5 B).

book_ref.quote: in which the OH group is replaced by some other group like X, OR, NH₂ etc.

blocks.prompt: 81 Besides ethanoyl chloride and HCl, the reaction of ethanoic acid with PCl₅ gives:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COOH + PCl₅ → CH₃COCl + HCl + POCl₃ (23.5 B).

book_ref.quote: Reaction with SOCl₂, PCl₃ and PCl₅

blocks.prompt: 82 The esterification of ethanoic acid with ethanol is carried out by heating in the presence of:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O (esterification) (23.5 B).

book_ref.quote: Carboxylic acids on heating with alcohols in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid produce esters.

blocks.prompt: 83 Lithium tetrahydridoaluminate(III) reduces carboxylic acids to:
blocks.explanation: The powerful reducing agent LiAlH₄ reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols (23.5 C).

book_ref.quote: reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols

blocks.prompt: 84 Which reducing agent will NOT reduce a carboxylic acid?
blocks.explanation: H₂/Ni and sodium tetrahydridoborate(III), NaBH₄, will not reduce carboxylic acids (23.5 C).

book_ref.quote: will not reduce carboxylic acids.

blocks.prompt: 85 According to the reduction box, which of the following is a reduction?
blocks.explanation: Reduction: gain of H₂ (or H⁻), loss of O, loss of X₂, gain of electrons, decrease in oxidation state (23.5 C box).

book_ref.quote: i. Gain of H₂ (or H⁻) ii. Loss of O or O₂

blocks.prompt: 86 Reduction of ethanoic acid with LiAlH₄ gives ethanol. How many [H] are needed per mole of acid?
blocks.explanation: CH₃COOH + 4[H] → CH₃CH₂OH + H₂O (23.5 C).

book_ref.quote: The powerful reducing agent lithium tetrahydridoaluminate (III)

blocks.prompt: 87 Methanoic acid acts as a strong reducing agent because:

options.text: its structure has an aldehydic (-CHO) portion as well as a carboxylic portion

blocks.explanation: Due to its structure (an aldehydic and a carboxylic portion) methanoic acid is oxidised by both weak and strong oxidising agents (23.5).

book_ref.quote: acts as a strong reducing agent

blocks.prompt: 88 The only monocarboxylic acid that gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent is:
blocks.explanation: Methanoic acid is the only monocarboxylic acid giving a silver mirror and a brick-red ppt with Fehling's solution (23.5).

book_ref.quote: Methanoic acid is the only monocarboxylic acid which gives positive silver mirror test

blocks.prompt: 89 With Fehling's solution, methanoic acid gives a brick-red precipitate of:
blocks.explanation: HCOOH + 2Cu(OH)₂ → Cu₂O + CO₂ + 3H₂O (brick red ppt); this identifies methanoic acid (23.5).

book_ref.quote: These reactions are used for the identification of methanoic acid.

blocks.prompt: 90 According to the oxidation box, which of the following is an oxidation?
blocks.explanation: Oxidation: loss of H₂ (or H⁻), addition of O, addition of X₂, loss of electrons, increase in oxidation state (23.5 box).

book_ref.quote: 4. Loss of electrons 5. Increase in Ox. State

blocks.prompt: 91 In the oxidation of ethanedioic acid by acidified KMnO₄, the oxidation state of carbon changes from:
blocks.explanation: Each C in HOOC-COOH is +3 and in CO₂ is +4, so carbon is oxidised (23.5).

book_ref.quote: results in the formation of carbon dioxide and water

blocks.prompt: 92 In the oxidation of ethanedioic acid by acidified KMnO₄, manganese changes from:
blocks.explanation: Mn is +7 in KMnO₄ and +2 in MnSO₄; it is reduced (23.5 equation).

book_ref.quote: The oxidation of ethanedioic acid with acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇

blocks.prompt: 93 From 2KMnO₄ + 3H₂SO₄ + 5H₂C₂O₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2MnSO₄ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O, the moles of KMnO₄ needed to oxidise 0.40 mol of ethanedioic acid are:
blocks.explanation: KMnO₄ : H₂C₂O₄ = 2 : 5, so 0.40 × 2/5 = 0.16 mol KMnO₄ (23.5 equation).

book_ref.quote: Methanoic acid gets oxidized with both weak as well as strong oxidizing agents

blocks.prompt: 94 The correct order of acidity is:
blocks.explanation: Carboxylic acids are considerably more acidic than phenols, and phenols more than alcohols (23.6).

book_ref.quote: Carboxylic acids are considerably more acidic than phenols

blocks.prompt: 95 The strength of an acid depends upon the:
blocks.explanation: The extent of ionization of an acid depends upon the stability of its conjugate base (23.6).

book_ref.quote: The acidic strength i.e, extent of ionization of an acid depends upon the stability of its conjugate base.

blocks.prompt: 96 Which statement is correct?

options.text: higher pKa means a stronger acid
lower Ka means a stronger acid
pKa does not depend on Ka
higher Ka or lower pKa means a stronger acid

blocks.explanation: Higher the Ka or lower the pKa, the stronger the acid (23.6 box).

book_ref.quote: Higher the Ka or lower the pKa, stronger will be the acid and vice versa.

blocks.prompt: 97 An acid has Ka = 1.0 × 10⁻³. Its pKa is:
blocks.explanation: pKa = –log Ka = –log(1.0 × 10⁻³) = 3 (23.6 box).

book_ref.quote: Higher the Ka or lower the pKa, stronger will be the acid

blocks.prompt: 98 According to Table 23.1, the pKa of a typical carboxylic acid RCOOH is about:
blocks.explanation: Table 23.1: RCOOH Ka 10⁻⁵, pKa 5; ArOH 10; HOH 14; R-OH 16 (23.6).

book_ref.quote: The relative values of acidity constant or ionization constant, Ka

blocks.prompt: 99 Using Table 23.1 (RCOOH Ka = 10⁻⁵, ArOH Ka = 10⁻¹⁰), a carboxylic acid is stronger than a phenol by a factor of about:

book_ref.quote: for a carboxylic acid, phenol or an alcohol

blocks.prompt: 100 The ethanoate ion is stabilised because:

options.text: it has a +I methyl group that adds charge
its negative charge is delocalised, decreasing its intensity on oxygen
its charge is fixed on one carbon atom

blocks.explanation: Delocalisation decreases the intensity of negative charge on oxygen, stabilising ethanoate so it is less likely to accept H⁺ (23.6).

book_ref.quote: the intensity of the negative charge on oxygen atom is decreased due to delocalization

blocks.prompt: 101 In the ethanoate ion, the negative charge is delocalised over:

options.text: the carbon and both oxygen atoms of -COO⁻

blocks.explanation: The ethanoate ion has no -COOH group; its electrons are delocalised over -COO⁻, the carbon and both oxygens (23.6, book correction).

book_ref.quote: its electrons are delocalised over the –COO⁻ group

blocks.prompt: 102 An electron donating group (+I effect) on a carboxylic acid:
blocks.explanation: A +I group intensifies the negative charge, destabilises the carboxylate ion and decreases acidity (23.6).

book_ref.quote: will tend to destabilize the carboxylate ion by intensifying the negative charge

blocks.prompt: 103 An electron withdrawing group (–I effect) increases the acidity of a carboxylic acid because it:

options.text: disperses the negative charge and stabilises the carboxylate ion

blocks.explanation: A –I group disperses the negative charge, stabilising the carboxylate ion and increasing acidity (23.6).

book_ref.quote: will tend to stabilize the carboxylate ion by dispersing its negative charge

blocks.prompt: 104 Methanoic acid is about 10 times stronger than ethanoic acid because:

options.text: hydrogen of methanoic acid has a –I effect
the CH₃ group of ethanoic acid has a +I effect
methanoic acid has two carboxyl groups
ethanoic acid has no carboxyl group

blocks.explanation: Hydrogen is the reference and has no –I effect; methanoic acid is stronger because the CH₃ of ethanoic acid has a +I effect (23.6, book correction).

book_ref.quote: methanoic acid is 10 times stronger acid than ethanoic acid

blocks.prompt: 105 Which of the following is the strongest acid?
blocks.explanation: The lowest pKa means the strongest acid; Cl₃C-COOH (0.64) is comparable to some mineral acids (23.6).

book_ref.quote: Trichloroacetic acid (Cl₃C-COOH) has a pKa of 0.64

blocks.prompt: 106 Chloroethanoic acid (pKa 2.86) is stronger than ethanoic acid (pKa 4.74). Its Ka is greater by a factor of about:

book_ref.quote: chloroacetic acid (ClCH₂-COOH) has a pKa of 2.86

blocks.prompt: 107 Using pKa = 1.26 for dichloroethanoic acid, its Ka is about:

book_ref.quote: Dichloroethanoic acid (Cl₂CH-COOH) is stronger, with a pKa of 1.26

blocks.prompt: 108 The order of acid strength of chloro-substituted ethanoic acids is:
blocks.explanation: Each Cl (–I) disperses the charge further; pKa 0.64 < 1.26 < 2.86 < 4.74 (23.6).

book_ref.quote: comparable in strength to some mineral acids

blocks.prompt: 109 Esters have lower boiling points than the corresponding alcohols and carboxylic acids because esters:

options.text: cannot form hydrogen bonds among their molecules

blocks.explanation: Unlike alcohols and acids, esters have no ability to form hydrogen bonds, so their boiling points are lower (23.7).

book_ref.quote: Esters, unlike alcohols and carboxylic acids have no ability to form the hydrogen bond.

blocks.prompt: 110 Ethyl ethanoate (b.p. 77 °C) compared with ethanoic acid (b.p. 118 °C) is:
blocks.explanation: A lower boiling point means a higher volatility; ethyl ethanoate is more volatile (23.7, book correction).

book_ref.quote: The b.p of ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₂H₅) is 77 °C

blocks.prompt: 111 Esters are less soluble or insoluble in water because of:
blocks.explanation: Lack of hydrogen bonds makes esters less soluble or insoluble in water (23.7).

book_ref.quote: Lack of hydrogen bonds makes esters less soluble/insoluble in water.

blocks.prompt: 112 Esters are used as flavouring agents in fruit drinks and sweets because they:
blocks.explanation: Many esters are liquids with sweet fruity smells; the fragrance and taste of fruits are due to esters (23.7).

book_ref.quote: Fragrance of fruits and their tastes are due to esters.

blocks.prompt: 113 The reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol in acidic medium to form an ester is known as:
blocks.explanation: This reaction is known as Fischer's esterification (23.7.1).

book_ref.quote: This reaction is known as Fischer's esterification.

blocks.prompt: 114 Propanoic acid and ethanol in acidic medium give:
blocks.explanation: CH₃CH₂COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃CH₂COOC₂H₅ (ethyl propanoate) + H₂O (23.7.1).

book_ref.quote: Propanoic acid and ethanol give ethyl propanoate

blocks.prompt: 115 Compared with the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol, the reaction of an acyl chloride with an alcohol:

options.text: is vigorous and goes to completion
needs concentrated H₂SO₄ and is slow

blocks.explanation: Acyl chlorides react vigorously with alcohols; the reaction goes to completion and gives no equilibrium mixture (23.7.1).

book_ref.quote: do not form an equilibrium mixture like the reaction between carboxylic acids and alcohols

blocks.prompt: 116 Ethanoyl chloride reacts with ethanol to form ethyl ethanoate and:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COCl + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + HCl (23.7.1).

book_ref.quote: Ethanoyl chloride and ethanol give ethyl ethanoate

blocks.prompt: 117 Phenyl esters are formed when phenol is warmed with:
blocks.explanation: Phenyl esters are formed when an acyl chloride is warmed with phenol (23.7.1).

book_ref.quote: Phenyl esters are formed when acyl chloride is warmed with phenol.

blocks.prompt: 118 Hydrolysis of methyl benzoate gives:
blocks.explanation: Aromatic esters are hydrolysed in the same manner, giving aryl carboxylic acids and alcohols (23.7.2).

book_ref.quote: An ester is hydrolyzed slowly to a carboxylic acid and an alcohol (or a phenol).

blocks.prompt: 119 Hydrolysis of an ester is:
blocks.explanation: An ester is hydrolysed slowly; the reaction is either acid- or base-catalysed (23.7.2).

book_ref.quote: The reaction is either acid or base-catalyzed.

blocks.prompt: 120 The functional group of acyl chlorides is:
blocks.explanation: Acyl chlorides have the functional group –COCl (23.8).

book_ref.quote: Acyl chlorides have the functional group –COCl.

blocks.prompt: 121 The general formula of saturated aliphatic acyl chlorides is:
blocks.explanation: Saturated aliphatic acyl chlorides have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COCl (23.8).

book_ref.quote: Saturated aliphatic acyl chlorides have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COCl.

blocks.prompt: 122 The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COCl is:
blocks.explanation: Acyl chlorides are named as alkanoyl halides; CH₃CH₂COCl is propanoyl chloride (23.8).

book_ref.quote: According to the IUPAC system, they are named as alkanoyl halides.

blocks.prompt: 123 Among the functional derivatives of carboxylic acids, the most reactive are:
blocks.explanation: Acyl chlorides are the most reactive functional derivatives, so they are used to prepare other derivatives (23.8).

book_ref.quote: acyl chlorides are the most reactive compounds among the functional derivatives of carboxylic acids

blocks.text: 23.9 Hydrolysis of Acyl Chlorides, Alkyl Chlorides and Aryl Chlorides

blocks.prompt: 124 Ethanoyl chloride is hydrolysed within a few minutes because its carbonyl carbon:

options.text: is part of a benzene ring
carries a large δ⁺ due to both O and Cl attached to it

blocks.explanation: Two highly electronegative atoms, O and Cl, on the carbon make it strongly δ⁺, so water attacks very fast (23.9).

book_ref.quote: Hence nucleophilic attack of H₂O on electrophilic carbon is so fast

blocks.prompt: 125 Chloroethane is hydrolysed more slowly than ethanoyl chloride because its carbon:

options.text: is part of a benzene ring
is attached to only one electronegative atom (Cl), so it has less δ⁺

blocks.explanation: In ethyl chloride the carbon is attached only to chlorine, so it gets less δ⁺ and the attack of water is comparatively slow (23.9).

book_ref.quote: the carbon gets comparatively less partial positive charge because it is attached to only chlorine atom

blocks.prompt: 126 Chlorobenzene does not undergo hydrolysis under these conditions because:

options.text: a lone pair of Cl is delocalised into the ring, giving the C-Cl bond double bond character

blocks.explanation: A lone pair on Cl takes part in delocalisation with the π electrons of the ring, giving C-Cl double bond character, so it does not break (23.9).

book_ref.quote: This will create a double bond character in C-Cl bond

blocks.prompt: 127 The order of ease of hydrolysis is:
blocks.explanation: Acyl chloride is fastest (minutes), alkyl chloride is slow, and chlorobenzene does not react (23.9).

book_ref.quote: The reactivity of acyl chlorides, alkyl chlorides and aryl (arene) chlorides can be compared

blocks.prompt: 128 Hydrolysis of ethanoyl chloride with water gives ethanoic acid and:
blocks.explanation: CH₃COCl + H₂O → CH₃COOH + HCl (23.9).

book_ref.quote: Hydrolysis of ethanoyl chloride, chloroethane and chlorobenzene

blocks.prompt: 129 In the hydrolysis of these chlorides, water acts as a:
blocks.explanation: Water makes a nucleophilic attack on the electrophilic (δ⁺) carbon (23.9).

book_ref.quote: So, the nucleophilic attack of water is comparatively slow
